_doc: Boss knockout cutscenes (Baki x Spike Spiegel, narrated Palahniuk). Beats run in order: stance -> slip -> xray -> finisher -> crowd -> closer. Narration is Duff at the bar, present tense (docs/voice.md). 'crowd' is a speaker-labelled line (gets that NPC's portrait). Boss defeat line from boss.gd plays after 'closer'. Keep {tokens}. See docs/knockout_cutscenes.md. "live": true = plays in game (pilot: gymbro).

husk.stance: He's streaming this to two hundred million people. My audience is a fryer and a guy named Hector. I bounce on my heels. I wave him in. Two fingers.
husk.slip: His rocket comes in slow. Everything is slow when you've worked a double. I lean six inches left. The rocket keeps going, toward its next funding round.
husk.xray: Fun fact: the human ego has no bones. It's held up by other people's money. My elbow finds it anyway. It makes the sound of a stock split.
husk.finisher: Every punch is a ticket. Every ticket gets fired. Nobody gets comped.
husk.crowd: Brittany: "He's gonna post about this. He is gonna post SO much about this."
husk.closer: I fix my apron. Somewhere a market dips. Nobody I know owns any of it.

bozos.stance: He has seventeen houses. I have one apartment and a cat who hates me. I roll my neck. I let my hands hang loose, like I'm waiting on a bus.
bozos.slip: His drones swarm in. I duck one, step through two, let the fourth hit the third. Teamwork. He's never seen it before.
bozos.xray: The human jaw has two hinges. His were installed by the lowest bidder. One knee, and both of them open for business.
bozos.finisher: You can't automate this. I checked. It's still just a guy with a spatula and nothing to lose.
bozos.crowd: Dolores: "Honey, that man just got returned to sender."
bozos.closer: Package delivered. Signature required. I sign it with my left hook.

fences.stance: He's buffering. I'm not. I tap my chest twice, open my hand, and wait. Patience is free. Everything else he sells.
fences.slip: A blue screen fills the room. I've seen worse at 2 AM on a POS terminal. I step around it like a puddle.
fences.xray: The spine is thirty-three vertebrae stacked like dirty plates. I clear the stack. Top to bottom. The way Dolores taught me.
fences.finisher: Ctrl. Alt. Delete. Three hits, in order, no updates required.
fences.crowd: Earl: "Kid didn't even spill his coffee."
fences.closer: He shuts down. Doesn't save his work. Nobody ever does.

baron.stance: His monocle costs more than my car. His car costs more than my life. I shrug off my jacket. I let it fall. I don't look where it lands.
baron.slip: He throws coins. Thirty-seven cents at a time. I catch a quarter out of the air and pocket it. Rent's due Monday.
baron.xray: Inherited wealth sits in the lower back. It's where the posture comes from. One kidney shot and three generations of it fold.
baron.finisher: This is what work feels like. I wanted you to know, just once, before you die old.
baron.crowd: {partner}: "Babe. BABE. Don't break the champagne tower, we can't afford the tower."
baron.closer: He calls for Mummy. Mummy doesn't come. Welcome to the rest of us.

donald.stance: He's talking. He's been talking for six minutes. I wait for a comma. There isn't one. I bounce, loose, and step in on a vowel.
donald.slip: He builds a wall. I go around it. Walls are like that. Ask anybody who's ever been in a kitchen.
donald.xray: The human hand has twenty-seven bones. His are smaller than mine. Everybody says so. My fist says so the loudest.
donald.finisher: Big league. Tremendous. The best knockout anybody's ever seen. People are saying.
donald.crowd: Brittany: "I'm putting twenty on 'he says it was rigged.'"
donald.closer: He calls it a win. Of course he does. I call it Tuesday.

ghoster.stance: Three years ago he left {partner} on read. Tonight he's left standing. I hold my hands low. I make him guess.
ghoster.slip: He vanishes. Classic. I don't chase. I wait at the spot he'll come back to. Guys like him always come back to the same spot.
ghoster.xray: There's a nerve in the ribs called the intercostal. It's the one that holds your excuses. I hit it, and all of them come out at once.
ghoster.crowd: {partner}: "...Okay, that was kind of hot. Don't tell anyone I said that."
ghoster.closer: He types something. Deletes it. Types it again. Some guys never learn to hit send.

gymbro.stance: He's two hundred and sixty pounds of protein powder and grievance. I'm one-ninety of coffee and spite. I bounce. Loose. Like nothing in me is load-bearing.
gymbro.slip: His curl comes around like a wrecking ball. I'm not where the ball lands. I never was. I'm already under his elbow, where the muscle ends and the guy begins.
gymbro.xray: Fun fact: a bicep is just a tendon with a marketing budget. Mine finds the tendon. It snaps like a ticket off the rail.
gymbro.finisher: You train for mirrors. I train for Saturday brunch. Brunch has never once skipped leg day.
gymbro.crowd: Brittany: "PAY ME. Everybody who bet on the abs, PAY ME."
gymbro.closer: He's crying. Not from pain. From missing a post. I let him have it. Grief is a muscle too.

djvape.stance: The bass is so loud my fillings buzz. I nod along. I find the beat. I wait for the drop like everybody else in the room.
djvape.slip: Vape cloud. Strawberry Mango Ice. I hold my breath and walk through it, the way I walk through the dish pit steam. Eyes open. Mouth shut.
djvape.xray: The inner ear is three tiny bones and a lot of fluid. She's been drowning hers for years. One open palm and the room tilts for her.
djvape.finisher: Three. Two. One. Nothing drops harder than you.
djvape.crowd: Dolores: "I've seen better sets at a funeral, sweetie."
djvape.closer: She asks if the fight counts as exposure. It does. She's exposed.

crypto.stance: He's standing on a rug. He's always standing on a rug. I keep my feet on the tile. I keep my hands where he can't price them.
crypto.slip: An NFT the size of a door comes at me. It has a monkey on it. I step aside and it hits nothing, which is exactly what it's worth.
crypto.xray: There's a ligament in the ankle that holds up a man's entire belief system. I sweep it. His whole portfolio leaves the ground.
crypto.crowd: Earl: "Back in my day we called that a pyramid. And a pyramid was a shape."
crypto.closer: He says he's up spiritually. I'm up four bucks. One of us is right.

willnot.stance: Forty floors. No shoes. Glass everywhere. He's limping and he's still talking. I slide my feet like the floor is ice, which is a trick you learn after one bad mop shift.
willnot.slip: He fires everything at once. Sprinklers. Vents. Bad attitude. I go low, then lower, then I'm behind him, like a server sneaking a plate out of the window.
willnot.xray: The bottom of the foot has twenty-six bones and a thousand nerve endings. He walked across a glass floor to get here. I don't hit the foot. I don't have to.
willnot.crowd: {partner}: "Is it over? Can we go home? I left the baby with Brittany."
willnot.closer: The tower goes quiet. Every ex, defeated. Every elevator, out of order. I take the stairs. Forty floors. It's still easier than brunch.

regular.stance: Earl has been coming here for thirty-one years. He's outlived three owners and a fire. He stands up slow. I give him the respect of standing still.
regular.slip: He swings like a man who learned in a war nobody remembers. I slip it and it still rings my ear. The coffee cups shiver on the counter.
regular.xray: An old man's heart is a fist that never unclenched. I don't hit it. I hit everything around it, so it can finally rest.
regular.finisher: Order up. Hash browns, scattered, smothered, covered. And you, Earl. Plated.
regular.crowd: Dolores: "Thirty-one years. Nobody's ever plated Earl."
regular.closer: He sits back down. He tips. Exact change. And one piece of advice I'm still trying to understand.

sendback.stance: He's sent back nine plates. The tenth plate is me. I set my feet. I don't garnish anything.
sendback.slip: He shoves the plate at me. I take it, turn, set it down on the pass without breaking stride. Twelve years on the line. Plates don't scare me.
sendback.xray: The tongue has ten thousand taste buds. His only ever tasted complaints. One uppercut and he tastes something new. It's humility. It's medium rare.
sendback.crowd: Dolores: "Told you to stop sending it back, hon."
sendback.closer: Five stars. Still no tip. Some things you can't beat out of a man. I try anyway, a little, in my heart.

coupon.stance: She has nine hundred coupons in a binder held shut by a rubber band and hate. I bow. You bow to a pro. Then you take her apart.
coupon.slip: She throws the binder. Coupons everywhere, like confetti at a sad wedding. I walk through it. Half of them are expired. All of them are hers.
coupon.xray: There's a muscle in the forearm called the flexor. It's the one that clips. Hers is the size of a ham. I tap it, and her whole hand forgets coupons exist.
coupon.finisher: The first one's full price. The second one's free.
coupon.crowd: Earl: "She tried that move on me in '98. Didn't work then either."
coupon.closer: She asks if there's a coupon for this. There isn't. There never is for the things that hurt.

allergy.stance: She's allergic to gluten, dairy, nuts and accountability. I wash my hands first. It's policy.
allergy.slip: She fakes a reaction. Hand to throat. Gasping. I've seen better at a dinner theater. I step around the performance.
allergy.xray: The human throat is a tube about an inch wide. Everything she's ever lied about goes down it. One jab to the solar plexus and the truth comes back up.
allergy.crowd: Dolores: "She ate a whole basket of rolls in booth four, baby. I watched her."
allergy.closer: She admits it. Free dessert. That's all it ever was. That's all it ever is.

camper.stance: He's been in booth six for four hours on one coffee. His laptop's at three percent. So's my patience. I roll my shoulders. I stand where the outlet is.
camper.slip: He swings his laptop bag like a flail. I let it pass, close enough to read the stickers. One says 'disrupt.' I plan to.
camper.xray: Fun fact: sitting for four hours shortens your hip flexors by about the length of a grudge. His snap like a charging cable.
camper.finisher: We close at two. It's two.
camper.crowd: Brittany: "He was on the wifi the whole fight. He's still on the wifi."
camper.closer: He leaves. He goes to the library. It's quieter there. It's free there. Nobody there will ever hit him.

bdaydad.stance: There are eleven kids, one cake and one dad who said 'yeet' on purpose. I take off my hat. Birthdays deserve respect.
bdaydad.slip: He sends the kids in first. Nuggets fly. I dodge a juice box, a party hat and Tanner, who bites. Tanner always bites.
bdaydad.xray: A grown man's dignity sits in his knees. That's why dads crouch so much at parties. One low kick and his folds into a lawn chair.
bdaydad.crowd: {partner}: "Okay, when {baby} turns one we are NOT doing a Waffle Haus party."
bdaydad.closer: The kids clap. They think it's part of the show. In a way, everything is part of the show.

dasher.stance: He's halfway to the door with a whole pie under his arm. I take one step. That's all it takes. He knows I've done this before.
dasher.slip: He runs. I don't. I cut the angle the way you cut a corner in a busy kitchen, and he runs straight into the space where I already am.
dasher.xray: Running away uses about two hundred muscles. Stopping uses just one, and it's mine.
dasher.crowd: Earl: "Should've paid for the pie, son. Pie's worth paying for."
dasher.closer: He pays. In cash. And the pie. I eat a slice on my break. It tastes like justice and margarine.
